name: LLM-narrative pressure long — bullish news-text narrative confirmed by price momentum
rationale: FIRST-CUT test of the LLM-NARRATIVE axis. Our own OpenRouter LLM scores each raw GDELT news headline CONTENT-ONLY and as-of its publish timestamp (no outcome reasoning, no dates, no price) into a typed signed-magnitude in [-1,1]; the day's headlines are aggregated (confidence-weighted) into a point-in-time daily 'net narrative pressure' series exposed under the feature name news_event_score. The hypothesis: when the day's news narrative is net-bullish (news_event_score > floor) AND price momentum confirms the move is already underway, the crowd narrative is corroborating a real trend rather than fading it; enter the intersection and hold until the narrative itself turns net-negative (cross_down exit) or risk limits hit. The momentum-confirmation leg guards against buying a one-day headline pop with no follow-through. Disconfirmers (in the cohort harness, ALL counted as trials in the SAME BH-FDR family): (a) a TIME-SHUFFLE placebo of the LLM scores — same marginal distribution, scrambled timing — MUST destroy the edge (if it reproduces, the LLM leaked the future or the timing is noise); (b) a momentum-only control — if it matches the candidate's deflated Sharpe, the LLM narrative adds no orthogonal information. tier1 + low-confidence until it clears the honest Gate OOS on a real holdout.
catalyst: LLM-scored daily news narrative is net-bullish (news_event_score > floor) while price momentum is positive
